title: 💬 Reported Speech

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body:
Reported speech (indirect speech) conveys what someone said without quoting them directly. In academic writing, it's essential for citing research.

Direct: The researcher said, "The results are significant."
Reported: The researcher stated that the results were significant.

sections.heading: Tense backshift
sections.body:
Present → Past: "is" → "was"
Present perfect → Past perfect: "has found" → "had found"
Past → Past perfect: "found" → "had found"
Will → Would: "will improve" → "would improve"
Can → Could: "can reduce" → "could reduce"

sections.heading: Reporting verbs (academic)
sections.body:
Neutral: stated, noted, observed, remarked
Claiming: argued, contended, maintained, asserted
Suggesting: suggested, proposed, indicated, implied
Agreeing: acknowledged, confirmed, concurred
Criticising: questioned, challenged, disputed, refuted

highlight: Using a variety of reporting verbs (not just "said") is a direct marker of Band 7+ Lexical Resource.

question: "Technology improves learning." → Which reported speech is correct?
options: She said that technology improved learning.
She said that technology will improve learning.
She said technology has improved learning.
correct: She said that technology improved learning.
explanation:
Present simple → Past simple in reported speech: "improves" → "improved"

The word "that" is optional but recommended in formal writing.

❌ "improves" — no tense shift (only acceptable in academic writing when the statement is still true)
❌ "will improve" — wrong tense shift
❌ "has improved" — present perfect, wrong here
hint: Tense backshift: present simple "improves" → past simple "improved".

sentence: The scientists _______ that rising sea levels _______ a significant threat to coastal cities.
explanation:
"Argued" is a sophisticated academic reporting verb — much stronger and more precise than "said".

"Posed a threat" is an academic collocation — you "pose" a threat/risk/challenge in formal writing.

Never use "told" without an object: "told us that" ✅ but "told that" ❌
hint: Use a formal reporting verb. "Pose a threat" is a fixed collocation.

instruction: Match each reporting verb to its meaning:

pairs.meaning: argued strongly that something is true
suggested as a hypothesis without proof

explanation: These Band 8+ reporting verbs each carry a specific stance. Choosing the right one shows both Lexical Resource and academic understanding — examiners notice the difference.

sentences.text: The study concluded that air pollution had increased over the decade.
The researcher told that the experiment was a success.
sentences.explanation:
"Tell" requires an object: "told US/HIM/THE CLASS that..."

✅ Correct options:
• "The researcher SAID that the experiment was a success."
• "The researcher TOLD US that the experiment was a success."

This is one of the most common grammar errors in IELTS Writing.

sentences.text: Critics argued that the policy would fail to address inequality.
